solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maybe churchwarden and kid briefly began to speak

parts.note: a churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay smoking pipe

indicators.note: briefly means the word for kid loses its final letter

parts.note: to kid is to fool, so a kid is a dupe

explanation.surface: A church official and a child together start talking, perhaps at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks churchwarden as an example of a pipe, not a church officer; 'briefly' cuts DUPE to DUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To pipe up is an idiom for starting to speak, often unexpectedly.

clue.text: Land job principally as carrier for Royal Mail

parts.note: a post is a job; principally signals it comes first, ahead of the word for land
to land something, such as a prize, is to bag it

explanation.surface: Getting a post office job, chiefly as a delivery person for Royal Mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principally' only says the job word leads; it picks no first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbag is the sack in which a postal worker carries letters, so it holds the mail.

clue.text: See car repairer pop across a north German river

indicators.note: across means the father word stretches over the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: pop and pater are both words for father
the Elbe is a river flowing through northern Germany

explanation.surface: A sightseer is told to go and see a mechanic, father spanning a river in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' just points the solver to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel beater is a tradesman who hammers out dents in car bodywork.

clue.text: Dickens hero forced into boring menial work

indicators.note: forced into means the hero is pushed inside the word for boring

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
Barnaby Rudge is the title hero of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A Dickens character is made to do tedious, lowly work.
explanation.definitionFit: Drudgery is hard, dull, servile labour, the same as menial toil.

clue.text: Old man cut soft fruit

indicators.note: cut means the fruit's name loses its last letter

parts.note: a papaw is a soft tropical fruit, another name for the papaya

explanation.surface: An elderly man slices up some soft fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Papa is an affectionate word for father, and 'old man' is slang for one's father.

clue.text: Dancing figures one's seen in celebrations

indicators.note: seen in means the one sits within the run of celebrations

parts.note: dos are parties; two of them, side by side, give the letters around the one
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A dance figure turns up at parties.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link. The I splits the parties, DOS and DOS, which is a fair reading of in, if a loose one.
explanation.definitionFit: A do-si-do is a square-dance move where partners circle back to back.

clue.text: Arty type translated title penned by Italian writer

indicators.note: penned by means the rearranged letters are enclosed by the writer's name

parts.note: Dante Alighieri wrote the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: translated means the letters of title are rendered into a different order

explanation.surface: A cultured sort renders a book title as written by an Italian author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' looks like a literary act, but it shuffles the five letters, giving ILETT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in the arts without professional commitment: an arty amateur.

clue.text: Leave group of fellows at the outset

parts.note: a set is a group of things or people

indicators.note: at the outset picks the opening letter of fellows

explanation.surface: A band of men departs right at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off is to depart on a journey, which is to leave.

clue.text: Expert lawyer, No 1 among barristers

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

indicators.note: No 1 among picks the first letter of barristers

explanation.surface: A skilled lawyer, the top barrister of the set.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab, as in 'dab hand', is someone very skilled at something.

clue.text: Poet, writer captured by Communists in revolution

indicators.note: captured by means the writer is held inside the other piece
in revolution means the word for Communists is turned round

parts.note: Reds are Communists
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: A poet, also a writer, is seized by revolutionary Communists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' suggests political upheaval but turns the word round, giving SDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Spender was a 20th-century English poet.

clue.text: Something wrong as hymn finishes early

indicators.note: finishes early means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: to hymn is to sing praises

explanation.surface: Something has gone wrong because the hymn has ended too soon.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin is a wrong act, a moral transgression.

clue.text: Friend tucked into fish ignoring starter; food's not tasty

indicators.note: tucked into means the friend goes inside the shortened fish
ignoring starter means the fish's first letter is dropped

parts.note: tuna is a fish
pal means friend
table can mean the food served, as in 'keeps a good table'; the 's is the link 'is'

explanation.surface: A friend, tucking into fish without a first course, finds the food unappealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring starter' reads as skipping the first course, but it drops the fish's first letter, leaving UNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpalatable means unpleasant to taste, so not tasty.

clue.text: Empty barge having to pull a large marine creature

indicators.note: empty means only the outside letters of barge are kept

parts.note: to lug is to pull or haul something heavy

explanation.surface: An empty barge has to drag a big sea animal along.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga is a white whale, and also a large sturgeon.

clue.text: Welshman takes ring road near small market town

parts.note: Taff is a nickname for a Welshman, after the River Taff
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A Welshman takes the ring road close to a little market town.
explanation.walkthrough: TAFF is a British nickname for a Welshman, from the River Taff in Cardiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford is the county town of Staffordshire, historically a market town.

clue.text: Performer's hesitation to appear in soap broadcast in Germany

indicators.note: to appear in means the hesitation goes inside the rearranged soap
broadcast means the letters of soap are scattered into a new order

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An actor hesitates before appearing in a soap opera shown in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' fits the TV surface but shuffles the four letters into OPAS. The 's after Performer is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera singer is a vocal performer on the operatic stage.

clue.text: Not mad to hoard silver now

indicators.note: to hoard means the silver is kept inside the phrase for not mad

parts.note: 'all there' is an idiom for being of sound mind
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: It is not crazy to stockpile silver at the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something 'all the rage' is highly fashionable, very much of the present moment.

clue.text: Fighters turn and go off course, badly overcome by poisonous fumes

indicators.note: overcome by means the other pieces are surrounded by the fumes

parts.note: gas, as in poison gas
a U-turn, so U can mean turn
to err is to stray from the right path
ill can mean badly, as in 'ill-treated'

explanation.surface: Soldiers turn round and stray off their route, struck down by gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Guerrillas are irregular fighters who wage small-scale war.

clue.text: Apparel twee pairs regularly sported

indicators.note: regularly means every second letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: Fussy pairs of outfits are on show.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of TWEE and PAIRS give the answer; 'sported' sits with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear as a noun means clothing, as in evening wear or menswear.

clue.text: Mishap, one probed by investigators near northern town

indicators.note: probed by means the investigators go inside the word for one

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
T is a map abbreviation for town

explanation.surface: An accident in which someone is questioned by detectives near a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is usually I, but here it is a card term, the ace; 'northern town' is two abbreviations, not a place.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unlucky event, a mishap.

clue.text: Record number at Spielberg movie comeback

indicators.note: comeback means the film's title is turned around

parts.note: E.T. is Steven Spielberg's 1982 film

explanation.surface: A record-breaking figure as a Spielberg film returns.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to write it down, to record it.

clue.text: New recording on air, Holst piece

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an air is a tune, so the word on top of the record is a melody

explanation.surface: A fresh recording of a Holst work is broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune, the Mystic, is a movement of Holst's suite The Planets.

clue.text: Political skill, say, shown by Conservative leader a lot

parts.note: to say is to state

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Conservative

parts.note: a raft of something is a large amount

explanation.surface: A Tory leader displays plenty of political skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Statecraft is the art of conducting government affairs.

clue.text: Current Hamlet production interrupted by onset of rain

indicators.note: interrupted by means the rearranged letters are broken by the extra letter
a production of a play reworks it, so the letters of Hamlet are rearranged
onset of picks the first letter of rain

explanation.surface: A current staging of Hamlet is disrupted when it starts to rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' sounds theatrical but rearranges the play's name into THEMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermal is a rising current of warm air used by gliders and birds.

clue.text: Nomad wanders over independent land

indicators.note: over places the rearranged letters above the next piece in this down entry
wanders means the letters of nomad move around

explanation.surface: A nomad roams across free territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a territory under a ruler's control, a realm or land.

clue.text: Thoughtlessly followed wicked predator

indicators.note: wicked suggests something twisted, so the letters of predator are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone mindlessly trailed an evil hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat or imitate without thought or understanding.

clue.text: I'll open online bank account as easy as pie, perhaps

indicators.note: open here means the I goes inside, opening up the bank's name

parts.note: Smile is a British internet-only bank, part of the Co-operative Bank
I'll is 'I will', giving the I

explanation.surface: Someone says opening an internet bank account will be very easy.
explanation.walkthrough: Smile was the Co-operative Bank's online-only brand in the UK; I goes in after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: 'As easy as pie' is an example of a simile, a comparison using 'as' or 'like'.

clue.text: Singer's solo finally drowned by loud noise

indicators.note: drowned by means the letter is submerged inside the noise

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of solo

explanation.surface: A singer's solo is drowned out at the end by a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Celine Dion is a Canadian pop singer.

clue.text: Blue material RN stitched on uniform

indicators.note: on places the uniform letter next to the rearranged letters

parts.note: Uniform is the radio alphabet word for U

indicators.note: stitched means the letters are sewn together in a new arrangement

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Navy-blue fabric from the Royal Navy is sewn onto a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultramarine is a deep, vivid blue pigment.

clue.text: Antipasto portion: single piece of asparagus, perhaps

indicators.note: portion means part of the word antipasto is taken

explanation.surface: A starter platter's share is just one spear of asparagus.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus tips are the tender heads of the spears, so one is an example of a tip.

clue.text: Fitness centre gets your money upfront

indicators.note: upfront means the front letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A health club demands payment in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A gym is a place for physical exercise and training.

clue.text: Cost in old money.say

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: say means the money word is spoken, giving letters that sound the same

parts.note: pence are coins, money

explanation.surface: The price in pre-decimal currency, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: An expense is a cost, money spent on something.

clue.text: Spontaneous 18A

definitions.meaning: unaffected and unforced, like an easy manner
18 across is a musical note; the sign restoring a note to unsharpened, unflattened pitch

explanation.surface: An impromptu record, a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural means unforced and spontaneous; in music a natural is a note neither sharp nor flat.
